answer.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure on SMB creates urgency, but exp_73 definitively showed that targeted discounting drives short-term signup at the cost of cohort survival and retention (-12% at 30 days). This contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for established customers, not for defending against churn in price-sensitive segments. Simplified onboarding and activation messaging both improve early engagement and retention. Given the immediate churn threat and the proven +6% activation and +1% retention lift from in-product activation messaging (exp_91), messaging offers a rapid, lower-cost response that addresses engagement friction without conceding margin or acquiring unprofitable cohorts. This preserves pricing power while giving at-risk accounts reason to engage more deeply with the product's value before they decide to leave. A standard experiment scope allows measurement of impact on at-risk cohorts without full-scale commitment.
